question.text: Vidya Capital Partners, a Cat II PE fund, observes a 'Bridge Round' opportunity at one of its portfolio companies. Per Chapter 9, the Bridge Round is BEST described as:

answer.text: A permanent capital injection from strategic corporates replacing early investors.
Short-term working capital financing between two rounds of equity fund-raising, provided by banks, debt funds or even VC funds.
A mandatory SEBI-defined bridge financing tranche for Cat II AIFs before deploying 75% of corpus.
A fully convertible instrument maturing on the IPO listing date.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9 defines Bridge Round as: 'Some companies may require short-term financing to fund their working capital requirements between two rounds of funding. This is known as a Bridge Round. Banks, Debt Funds or even Venture Capital Funds provide such working capital funds.' The Trap: Option A confuses bridge with strategic/permanent capital. Option C invents a fictitious SEBI tranche rule. Option D describes a Mezzanine Pre-IPO convertible, not a bridge. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests the same definition from a client-education angle. XIX-C is now-superseded all-cat. XXIV (AML) and III-A/C (Compliance) don't touch this term.
